html:
SMTO-ART-0017 — SMTO didn't recognize that file retention choice

GUID: 8ccc413a-8382-4f3d-b9b2-cd3a8fe66ac1
Slug: artifact-retention-invalid
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO only accepts its listed choices for how long to keep a conversation's saved files. The choice sent wasn't one of them, so your retention setting stayed the same.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload SMTO in your browser. An old open page can send a choice the server no longer accepts.
  2. Open Artifacts from this run, find Artifact retention for this conversation, and choose Follow conversation retention, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or Keep until deleted. These are the only retention choices SMTO accepts.
  3. If you set retention from a script or another tool, change it to send one of these exact values: conversation, 7, 30, 90 or forever. Any other value is refused and the setting is left unchanged.

What success looks like

  • The list shows 'Saved.' followed by the retention explanation, and your choice stays selected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep sending the same value; it will be refused every time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The artifact-retention update was rejected because the policy is not one of the supported values: conversation, 7, 30, 90 or forever.

What this means

  • Retention settings validation receives a policy outside the supported POLICIES set. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Retention settings validation receives a policy outside the supported POLICIES set.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested policy with current advertised settings.

How to fix it

  • Send a policy value from POLICIES in agent_runtime/artifacts/maintenance.py (conversation, 7, 30, 90 or forever) to the conversation's artifact-retention PUT endpoint. If the browser sent another value, reload the page so it uses the current artifacts.js selector.
  • Choose a retention policy advertised by the current artifact settings.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An intentional supported policy passes validation and existing ownership protections remain active.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
